bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

news.label: Sin señales
news.summary: No hay anuncios ni reportes de trabajos de apertura en los Back Bowls. Vail abrió la temporada el 13 de noviembre con terreno limitado y el pronóstico solo trae nevadas ligeras esta semana.

sections.Key Messages:
- A quick moving system will bring snow to the mountains and a
  rain/snow mix for the valleys Monday morning through Monday
  night, with the San Juans favored with 2-4 inches.
- Active weather remains possible late Thanksgiving week, but
  some details still remain uncertain. Stay tuned for updates to
  timing and impacts as they become available.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 926 PM MST Sun Nov 22 2026
QUICK MOVING SYSTEM FOR MONDAY:
Mid and high level clouds continue to stream across the area
from the west, which should help keep overnight temperatures
from bottoming out like last night with limited radiational
cooling. This cloud cover is all ahead of an open wave trough
pushing through the Great Basin. This fast moving trough will
track across eastern Utah and western Colorado Monday morning
through Monday night with the trough axis pushing across the
Divide during Monday evening rush hour. Southwest flow will
focus precipitation across the Four Corners with the San Juans
being favored for accumulating snowfall before the low lifts
across the central mountain corridor with some wraparound
precipitation into Vail Pass by Monday night/early Tuesday
morning. QG forcing and steep lapse rates Monday afternoon will
promote periods of heavier snowfall across the mountains at
times, but overall accumulations look to remain below advisory
levels in the 2 to 4 inch range with the San Juans being
favored. Central and southern areas seem favored for showers
with snow in the mountains and a rain/snow mix in the valleys.
Could be some messy conditions at the passes, especially late
Monday afternoon into Monday evening so exercise caution if
traveling.
DRY WEATHER THROUGH MIDWEEK, POTENTIALLY ACTIVE AGAIN LATE WEEK:
Skies will clear by Tuesday morning with northerly flow behind
the departing trough as a high pressure ridge moves in from the
west. This will lead to dry conditions and much colder
temperatures Tuesday night as efficient radiational cooling
takes place. A weak shortwave trough looks to move through on
Thanksgiving Day but QG forcing shows signs of splitting with
not much impact to the area. With a large area of high pressure
building off the SoCal coast and Desert Southwest, the northern
stream looks to remain active with systems moving through the
Pacific Northwest and Northern Rockies. This potentially keeps
northwest flow across the area, potentially feeding moisture
into the Park Range for favored orographics late this week into
the coming weekend. There is some disagreement on how this
evolves but potential exists for active weather during this
timeframe with impacts particularly to the Park Range. Overall
with ridging mid to late week, temperatures look to warm up to
around 5 to 10 degrees above normal.
sections.Aviation:
Issued at 1043 PM MST Sun Nov 22 2026
Mid and high level clouds will move into the area shortly as a
weather system approaches from the southwest. Impacts from this
system become possible at KTEX and KDRO around 12Z, then at
KMTJ, KGJT, KRIL, KASE, KGUC, and KEGE in the morning or
afternoon. Lower clouds and snow, rain, or a rain and snow mix
could cause drops below ILS breakpoints and MVFR/IFR conditions
at impacted sites. Otherwise, VFR conditions are expected. Winds
will generally be light.
